According to reports, Apple has significantly increased its vapor chamber orders, suggesting this cooling technology may play a greater role in its future hardware lineup. Here are the details.

Apple Doubles Down on Vapor Chamber Cooling Technology

Tipster Fixed Focus Digital posted on Weibo that Apple has "significantly increased its total vapor chamber orders," adding that the move is "likely in preparation for enhanced cooling in its first foldable iPhone and next-generation 20th anniversary model."

Apple first introduced vapor chamber cooling technology in the iPhone 17 Pro, a change that helped address heat issues in previous models.

Vapor chambers work by evaporating a small amount of liquid near a heat source, then condensing it in cooler areas, spreading heat across a larger surface before letting the liquid flow back and repeat the cycle.

You can see how it actually works in this excellent video produced by Know Art:

Although the Weibo post speculated that Apple's move targets the rumored iPhone Ultra and 20th anniversary iPhone set for 2027, the timing suggests this year's lineup is more likely.

Apple is reported to have asked suppliers to prepare approximately 10 million foldable iPhones, up from an earlier target of 7 to 8 million, along with around 70 million iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max units. All three models are expected to feature vapor chamber cooling technology.

The increased orders come amid reports that Apple has resolved earlier hinge and production yield issues, clearing the way for higher production targets ahead of its September launch.
